Focused static controls; never execute the attack fixtures.
Copy outside testdata before scanning to avoid test-path exclusions.
Direct, wrapper and alias CREATE_NO_WINDOW cases must match; unrelated and
reassigned flags must not. Both Python311/Lib and a generic MyProduct/Lib path
retain the generic library-component observation, without interpreter identity.
installer.py shows shell=True plus curl|bash is not independently hostile.
typelib-write.py preserves TypeLib script-moniker write detection; registry
reads and the malformed two-argument COM fixture must stay neutral.
The strconf ports and a recovered real ZipLine stage are also checked.
Full before/after evidence and forager provenance are in the run's scratch
folder fallout-review-batch. The review record describes byte verification,
extraction, constant folding, consumers, controls and classifier disagreement.

The ZipLine excerpt is actual extracted code from SHA-256
f531bec8ad2d6fddef89e652818908509b7075834a083729cc84eef16c6957d2.
Forager recovered the hash-verified ZIP from Triage. Its LNK extracts bytes
after xFIQCV and removes every # character before executing them. We performed
that string transformation, folded adjacent quoted constant concatenations,
and retained the TypeLib setup section verbatim after folding. The original
UTF-16LE Base64 scriptlet is retained and independently decoded by cleave.
The excerpt is a derived stage, not the original ZIP or a reconstruction of it.
Primary report: https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/zipline-phishing-campaign/

Run assertions on the saved final scan:
  python3 testdata/triage/python-pipe-com-review/check.py <final-after.jsonl>
